candidates.teaser: Nine experienced hikers vanished on a mountain — and when rescuers found them, the evidence made absolutely no sense.
candidates.video_title: 9 Hikers Died — The Evidence Made No Sense
candidates.video_description: In 1959, nine skilled Soviet hikers were found dead on a Ural mountain under impossible circumstances. Their tent was cut open from the inside, they fled barefoot into minus-30°C cold, and one body was missing its tongue. The case was classified for decades.
candidates.script: Nine experienced hikers cut their tent open from the inside and ran barefoot into minus-30 degree cold — and nobody knows why. It was 1959, in the Soviet Ural Mountains. Rescuers found the bodies scattered across the snow. One woman was missing her tongue. Two victims had chest fractures so severe it looked like they'd been hit by a car — yet there were no external wounds. The Soviet government classified the files for 30 years. What do you think actually happened up there?

candidates.teaser: In just three days, an entire species lost half its global population — and science had no explanation for two years.
candidates.video_title: Half a Species Died in 3 Days — Nobody Knew Why
candidates.video_description: In May 2015, over 200,000 saiga antelopes collapsed and died across Kazakhstan in less than 72 hours. The die-off wiped out 60% of the entire world population of the species. For two years, scientists were completely baffled by the cause.
candidates.script: In May 2015, over 200,000 antelopes dropped dead across Kazakhstan in less than 72 hours. Not some of them — 60% of the entire species on Earth, gone in three days. Mothers, calves, entire herds. No predator, no poison, no obvious disease. Scientists stood in fields of carcasses with no answers. Two years later they finally identified the cause — a bacteria the animals had harmlessly carried for centuries, suddenly turned lethal. The trigger? A two-degree shift in temperature and humidity. Climate changed the math, and a species nearly vanished.

candidates.topic: The Stockholm Syndrome Origin — Norrmalmstorg Robbery
candidates.teaser: Hostages held at gunpoint for six days did something so bizarre that psychiatrists had to invent a brand new condition to describe it.
candidates.video_title: Hostages Defended Their Captor — Psychiatry Changed Forever
candidates.video_description: In 1973, four bank employees were held hostage in a Stockholm vault for six days. By the end, they feared the police more than the robber holding them captive — and one hostage later got engaged to him. The condition now affects millions of abuse victims worldwide.
candidates.script: Four hostages spent six days locked in a bank vault with a convicted criminal — and by day three, they were protecting him from police. It was Stockholm, 1973. The robber, Jan-Erik Olsson, demanded a getaway car and his prison friend. Instead he got a six-day standoff. The hostages started lying to negotiators. One woman later got engaged to him. A psychiatrist watching the case had to create an entirely new diagnosis just to explain what he was witnessing. That condition now has a name — and it affects millions of abuse victims alive today.

candidates.topic: The Grandfather Paradox — Time Travel Physics
candidates.teaser: Physicists don't actually say time travel is impossible — they say something far stranger instead.
candidates.video_title: Physicists Don't Say Time Travel Is Impossible
candidates.video_description: The grandfather paradox has stumped philosophers for decades, but quantum physicists have a deeply unsettling solution: you can go back in time, but the universe will subtly rearrange events to prevent any paradox from occurring. Free will may not survive the equation.
candidates.script: Physicists don't say time travel is impossible — they say the universe would cheat to stop you from breaking it. Go back and try to prevent your own birth, and according to quantum models, reality would subtly rearrange every event just enough to make sure you fail. Not by force — by probability. Every path that creates a paradox quietly becomes the least likely outcome. The universe isn't blocking you. It's just making sure you never quite succeed. Whether that means free will is an illusion is a question nobody has answered yet.

candidates.topic: The Stendhal Syndrome — Art-Induced Physical Collapse
candidates.teaser: Hundreds of tourists visit Florence's hospitals every year — not from illness, but from looking at paintings.
candidates.video_title: Some Paintings Are So Beautiful They Send People to Hospital
candidates.video_description: Stendhal Syndrome is a documented psychosomatic condition where exposure to highly concentrated art causes dizziness, rapid heartbeat, hallucinations, and fainting. Florence, Italy reports dozens of cases annually, mostly at the Uffizi Gallery. The French author Stendhal first described it in 1817 after nearly collapsing in a church.
candidates.script: Tourists in Florence, Italy are regularly rushed to hospital after staring at paintings — and it's a medically documented condition. It's called Stendhal Syndrome. The Uffizi Gallery sees dozens of cases every year: rapid heartbeat, dizziness, hallucinations, fainting — all triggered by art. The French author Stendhal described it first in 1817 after nearly collapsing inside a church in Florence. Doctors believe extreme beauty overwhelms the nervous system. The city has a dedicated protocol for it. Is that a flaw in human perception — or proof that art is more powerful than we admit?
